title: The surroundings of the interacting galaxy NGC 5291
caption: The interacting galaxy NGC 5291 and its surroundings, imaged by the Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image from ESO's Very Large Telescope shows the aftermath of a galactic collision that happened 360 million years ago. At the center is the elliptical galaxy NGC 5291, surrounded by debris thrown out in the crash.
Among that debris is a young dwarf galaxy, which shows up as a bright clump on the right-hand side of the picture. ESO describes it as both rare and mysterious.

Galaxies like it are expected to have been common in the early Universe. Those distant examples, however, are usually too faint and too far away for current telescopes to observe. Finding one close enough to study in detail gives astronomers a valuable chance to learn about a type of galaxy that may have been widespread long ago. NGC 5291 lies in the constellation of Centaurus, and the picture was made with the FORS2 instrument on the VLT.

understand.summary: This image comes from the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, using V, R and I filters that span visible and near-infrared light. The colors assigned to each filter are not published.
understand.eye: The debris and the dwarf galaxy are far too faint to see by eye. They show up only because a large telescope gathered light over long exposures.
